newsitem.title: USA: US Sen. D'Amato to introduce new bank regulations.
newsitem.headline: US Sen. D'Amato to introduce new bank regulations.

text.p: Senate Banking Committee Chairman Alfonse D'Amato said Thursday he will introduce legislation aimed at changing how banks, securities firms and insurance companies are regulated.

"Simply put, under this system the SEC will regulate securities activities, bank regulators will regulate bank products and activities, and state insurance regulators will regulate insurance activities," the New York Republican said.
The legislation follows the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency's approval of rules late last fall that would allow banks to engage in an array of activities, including insurance sales.
The lawmaker faulted the OCC for taking such a bold step without legislation directing such a move.

"Above all, I am deeply troubled and concerned that the Comptroller of the Currency's agressive actions may, once again, subject federally insured banks to excessive risks and expose the bank insurance funds, and therefore taxpayers, to unnecessary liability," D'Amato said.
The lawmaker told U.S. Comptroller Eugene Ludwig at a hearing Thursday that his agency's move "undermines the dual banking system."
"The comptroller is deliberately consolidating power within his agency by first approving new powers for national banks and then asserting the authority to regulate such activities," he said.
